title: Imam Bayildi
subtitle: Turkish baked aubergine stuffed with onion and tomato
excerpt: Whole aubergines slit and filled with sweet slow-cooked onions, garlic, and tomato, then baked in olive oil until completely soft. A dish that improves with resting.
sourceNotes: Ottoman-era Turkish dish; the name translates as 'the imam fainted', reputedly from the generous use of olive oil. Baked version is most common across Turkey and the Balkans.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made 1 to 2 hours ahead and served at room temperature. The filling soaks into the aubergine as it rests and the flavour deepens.

content.text: Imam bayildi is a stuffed aubergine dish baked low and slow in olive oil. The aubergine must be completely soft all the way through. A firm centre means it needs more time or more oil in the base of the tin.
Heat the oven to 180C. Cut a deep slit lengthways down each aubergine, leaving the ends intact. Open the slit gently to form a pocket. Salt the inside and leave for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat 4 tablespoons of oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onions with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes until very soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, paprika, and cinnamon. Cook for 2 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes, tomato puree, and sugar. Cook for another 8 minutes until the tomatoes break down. Season and stir in the parsley.
Pour 3 tablespoons of olive oil into the base of the roasting tin. Lay the aubergines cut side up. Spoon the filling generously into each pocket.
Pour the water around the aubergines and drizzle the remaining olive oil over the top.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for another 15 minutes until the aubergines are completely collapsed and soft.
Leave to rest for at least 15 minutes before serving. Squeeze lemon juice over the top. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The aubergine flesh is still firm after baking.
items.cause: The oven temperature was too low, or the foil was removed too early.
items.fix: Cover again with foil and return to the oven for another 15 to 20 minutes. Add a splash more water to the tin if the base looks dry.

items.cause: The tomatoes cooked down too far before going into the tin.
items.fix: Add a splash of water to the filling before stuffing the aubergines. The liquid steams the flesh from the inside as it bakes.

items.symptom: The skin of the aubergine is tough.
items.cause: The aubergines were too large, or did not have enough oil.
items.fix: Choose medium aubergines for this dish. Use enough olive oil to lightly coat the skin before baking.
